title: Mutations in electrogenic genes can produce coordinated, long-range anatomical change

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Mutations in electrogenic genes can produce coordinated, long-range anatomical change

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because the same membrane-voltage dynamics can be produced by many ion-channel combinations and bioelectric states act across tissue distances, evolution can swap channels freely, and simple mutations in electrogenic genes can cause long-range, highly coordinated changes in anatomy (supported by KCNH8 and a connexin in an evolutionary shift of fish fin morphology).

fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: evolution is free to swap out channels and explore the bioelectrical state space: simple mutations in electrogenic genes can exert very long-range, highly coordinated changes in anatomy.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems”. Scope: Animal morphological evolution, e.g. fish fins

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-28: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public sequence and developmental data can test named fish examples and selected genotype-phenotype associations. They do not yet establish the general interchangeability of channels or the breadth of coordinated effects.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Associate electrogenic variants with spatially distributed fin-shape changes, test causality in existing perturbation data, and compare whether diverse channel genotypes converge on equivalent voltage and morphology states.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Few evolutionary transitions have matched genotype, voltage, and whole-anatomy data.

Long-range coordination can arise through downstream developmental pathways.

The freedom to swap channels is broader than individual examples.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Zebrafish phenotype databases record anatomical effects of mutations in some potassium-channel genes, which can test the narrower claim that electrogenic mutations can change morphology in a coordinated way. The evolutionary example is a candidate-gene expression result during fin outgrowth, and differential expression does not show that a mutation caused the species difference. Public data therefore cover a related genetic possibility and leave the historical case weakly tested.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether mutations in electrogenic genes produce coordinated, multi-site anatomical changes, using zebrafish genotype-phenotype records, and separately test whether KCNH8 or a connexin is causal in the fish fin shift rather than merely differentially expressed.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Zebrafish fin mutants do not establish the evolutionary swap of channels in the swordtail case.

The cited fish-fin result identifies KCNH8 and a connexin in a transcriptome of a developing ornament, which is expression rather than a demonstrated causal mutation.

A raw RNA-seq accession for that study was not confirmed here, so the expression list cannot be assumed reanalyzable from a named archive.
